cli.usage:
codr: your own git forge

Usage:
  codr init [--dir DIR]                         create config.toml, data dir, DB and host key
  codr migrate [--check]                        apply DB schema (append-only)
  codr serve                                    run the SSH + HTTP servers and the hook socket
  codr admin user add NAME [--email E] [--admin] [--lang ms-MY|en-US]   password read from stdin
  codr admin user ls · user passwd NAME (password from stdin) · user 2fa-off NAME   recovery; signs the person out everywhere
  codr admin org add NAME --owner USER · org ls   organisations (members and teams: /org/NAME)
  codr admin key add NAME --title TITLE          public key read from stdin
  codr admin key ls NAME · key rm NAME ID
  codr admin token add NAME [--name N] [--scopes repo:read,repo:write] [--days D]   HTTPS token, shown ONCE
  codr admin token ls NAME · token rm NAME ID
  codr admin repo add OWNER/NAME [--public] [--desc TEXT] [--branch main]
  codr admin repo import OWNER/NAME URL [--token] [--interval MIN] [--public]   mirror from a URL (token from stdin)
  codr admin mirror ls · mirror sync OWNER/NAME|--all · mirror rm OWNER/NAME
  codr admin repo ls [OWNER]
  codr admin repo rm OWNER/NAME --yes
  codr admin repo desc OWNER/NAME TEXT           replace the one-line description (empty TEXT clears it)
  codr admin github import OWNER/NAME [--meta DIR] · github import --all --meta ROOT   issues, pull requests and comments from GitHub
  codr admin collab add OWNER/NAME USER --role read|write|admin
  codr admin protect add OWNER/NAME PATTERN [--allow-force] [--allow-delete] [--require-checks]   protected branches (glob)
  codr admin protect ls OWNER/NAME · protect rm OWNER/NAME PATTERN
  codr admin setting ls · setting set KEY VALUE   product settings (live, no restart)
  codr doctor                                   check the install (config, DB, git, hooks, key, disk, repos, mirrors)
  codr backup [--with-mirrors] DIR · codr restore BACKUP --dir EMPTY_DIR   consistent snapshot; restore = identical instance (mirrors refilled from source)
  codr cloud ls · cloud run · cloud restore --endpoint URL --bucket NAME --access-key ID --dir EMPTY_DIR   backups in your own S3 bucket (secret + recovery key from the environment)
  codr version

Config: --config FILE or CODR_CONFIG (default ./config.toml). Language: CODR_LANG.

landing.title: Codr · Self-hosted git forge in one Go binary
landing.description: Codr is a self-hosted git forge in one Go binary. Plain bare repositories on disk, SSH and HTTPS, issues, pull requests and CI, in Malay and English.
landing.nav.label: Main navigation
landing.hero.eyebrow: Self-hosted git forge · Built in Malaysia
landing.hero.lead: Codr keeps your git repositories on a server you run, with SSH, HTTPS, issues, pull requests and CI. One binary, one data folder, an interface in Malay and English.
landing.figure.label: A three-dimensional commit graph that forms the C of the Codr mark
landing.figure.caption: From the front, the letter C. Scroll and it turns into history: branches leave and merge back, and each pulse is a push arriving.
landing.features.title: What already runs
landing.features.lead: Everything below is running at %s today.
landing.f1.t: Clone and push over SSH or HTTPS
landing.f1.d: SSH keys and tokens for every user. Protected branches refuse force pushes, and the push size limit is a setting.
landing.f2.d: Labels, comments and reviews. A merge checks for conflicts first and never overwrites a push that lands at the same moment.
landing.f3.t: Mirrors from GitHub or any URL
landing.f3.d: Repositories refresh on a schedule. Source tokens are encrypted in the database and never appear in logs.
landing.f4.d: codr backup takes a consistent snapshot. On this server that snapshot is restored again every night as a drill.
landing.f5.d: File tree, syntax highlighting, history, blame, in-repository search and READMEs with their images.
landing.f6.t: One command to check it all
landing.f6.d: codr doctor checks the config, database, git, hooks, keys and disk space. One line per check.
landing.data.title: Your repositories stay plain git
landing.data.lead: Codr does not convert your repositories into a format of its own. Each one is a bare git repository inside the data folder. If the server stops, you can still clone straight from disk.
landing.data.box: The data folder on the server
landing.data.p1d: The SQLite database and the repositories live together. Copy the folder, or use codr backup for a snapshot while the server runs.
landing.data.p2d: No Postgres, Redis or queue to look after. The SSH and HTTPS servers and the mirror scheduler run in one process.
landing.fit.title: Who it is for
landing.fit.yes1: Solo developers who want their code on their own machine.
landing.fit.yes2: Small teams that need code review, CI and shared organisations without a subscription.
landing.fit.yes3: Anyone who wants to read and understand the forge they run.
landing.fit.no1: Large organisations with thousands of users and compliance audits.
landing.fit.no2: Teams that need a package or container registry beside their code.
landing.fit.no3: Anyone looking for a hosted service. Codr runs on a server you look after.
landing.install.title: Install on your server
landing.install.lead: You need Linux (amd64 or arm64) and git 2.40 or newer. Download the release binary, or build it with Go 1.27. The SSH and HTTPS servers start with one command.
landing.install.licence: Licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later. If you change the server code, share those changes with the people who use your server.
landing.end.title: See it for yourself
landing.end.lead_demo: An example repository on the owner's forge is open without an account: files, history, issues and pull requests.
landing.og_alt: Codr: a self-hosted git forge in one Go binary

landing.faq.title: Before you install
landing.faq.gitea.q: Is Codr an alternative to Gitea or Forgejo?
landing.faq.gitea.a: Yes, for one person or a small team who want a forge they can read end to end. Gitea and Forgejo do much more: package registries, Actions-compatible CI, federation work in Forgejo and large communities. Codr is smaller: one Go binary, one SQLite file, plain bare repositories, an English and Malay interface, and CI jobs that run with no network by default. If you need packages or a plugin ecosystem, choose Gitea or Forgejo.
landing.faq.postgres.q: Does Codr need Postgres, Redis or a queue?
landing.faq.postgres.a: No. Codr keeps its data in one SQLite file next to plain bare git repositories. Copy the data folder, or run codr backup while it is running for a consistent snapshot.
landing.faq.licence.a: AGPL-3.0-or-later. You may use, change and host it, also at work. If you change the server and let other people use it over a network, share your changes with them under the same licence.
landing.faq.install.q: What do I need to run it?
landing.faq.install.a: Linux on amd64 or arm64 and git 2.40 or newer. Download the release binary and check it against SHA256SUMS, then run codr init and codr serve. Building from source needs Go 1.27. Docker is only needed for CI.
landing.faq.github.q: Can I move my repositories from GitHub?
landing.faq.github.a: Yes. Codr mirrors a GitHub repository and imports its issues and pull requests with their original numbers, so links like #12 keep working.
landing.faq.who.a: %s at %s, in Malaysia. Codr has hosted its author's own code since October 2026.

ui.cloud.title: Backups to your cloud
ui.cloud.intro: Every run takes a full snapshot, encrypts it with your recovery key, uploads it to your bucket, downloads it again and checks that it opens and matches. Old archives beyond the number you keep are deleted.
ui.cloud.no_secret_key: This install has no auth.secret_key in config.toml, so nothing can be stored sealed. Run codr init on a new folder or add a key, then restart.
ui.cloud.key_created: Your new recovery key. Write it down or put it in a password manager now.
ui.cloud.key_once: It is shown this one time. Without it the archives in your bucket cannot be opened, by you or by anyone. Archives made with an earlier key still need that earlier key.
ui.cloud.endpoint_hint: Any S3-compatible service: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, AWS S3 or your own MinIO. Use the bucket's endpoint without the bucket name.
ui.cloud.secret_kept: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
ui.cloud.key_explain: Archives are encrypted with this key before they leave the server. The bucket provider never sees your code. Keep a copy away from this server: if the server is lost, the key and the bucket are all you need.
ui.cloud.restore_explain: On any machine with git and the codr binary, this downloads the newest archive, opens it with your recovery key and rebuilds the install in an empty folder. Put the bucket secret and the key in the environment, never on the command line.
ui.cloud.restore_cmd:
export CODR_CLOUD_SECRET='…' CODR_RECOVERY_KEY='…'
codr cloud restore --endpoint %s --region %s --bucket %s --prefix %s --access-key %s --dir /srv/codr

landing.next.webhooks.d: Every push, issue, comment, review and status sent to your own URL, signed with HMAC, retried with backoff, and never to a private address unless you allow it.
landing.next.notify.d: A bell and an optional email for the threads you opened, joined, were mentioned in or watch, and never about a repository you cannot read.
landing.next.twofa.d: TOTP with any authenticator app, one-time recovery codes, and a list of signed-in browsers you can end.
landing.next.api.d: The same tokens as git, capped by their scope, with commit statuses for your CI runners and a machine-readable description.
landing.next.lfs.d: Large files over HTTPS and SSH, checked by hash on upload and carried through forks, backups and restores.
landing.next.wiki.d: Markdown pages beside the code, each change a commit, two editors never overwriting each other, and the whole wiki one git clone away.

landing.design.title: How Codr is built
landing.design.description: The choices behind Codr: one binary, real git, one SQLite file, one permission decision, CI outside the forge.
landing.next.ci.d: Every push runs the jobs in .codr/ci.toml in a container with no network. Results show on the commit and the pull request, and a protected branch can wait for all of them to pass.
landing.next.flow.d: Issue and pull request assignees, fixes #12 closing issues, squash or rebase merges, and your own activity log.

ui.oidc.intro: OpenID Connect for organisations that already have central accounts (Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra, Keycloak and others). Someone gets in only when the email the provider has VERIFIED equals the email of an existing Codr account. No account is created, and Codr's 2FA is still asked.
